text: 224 Oceana is an asteroid located in the asteroid belt. It was discovered by Austrian astronomer Johann Palisa on 30 March 1882 in Vienna and was named after the Pacific Ocean. Based on its spectral characteristics, it is classified as an M-type asteroid, though it is not metallic. Photometric observations of 224 Oceana at the Pulkovo Observatory produced a light curve indicating a rotation period of 9.401 ± 0.001 hours and a brightness variation of 0.09 ± 0.01 in magnitude. The asteroid was one of five minor planets studied in the 1993 research project titled Transition Comets -- UV Search for OH Emissions in Asteroids, which involved amateur astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope.
